newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Blast, blaze hit Czech oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Blast, blaze hit Czech oil refinery.

text.p: An explosion and fire ripped through storage tanks at the Litvinov oil refinery in the northern Czech Republic on Saturday but nobody was injured, the Interior Ministry said.

But the Czech news agency CTK said that production had been cut due to the blaze at the refinery. It belongs to Czech refining company Ceska Rafinerska a.s. which is 49 percent owned by a consortium comprising Du Pont de Nemours unit Conoco, Royal Dutch/Shell, and Italy's Agip SpA.
An Interior Ministry statement said the blaze had been reported to the fire brigade at 00.35 a.m. (2335 GMT Friday). "The spread of the fire was probably caused by an explosion," it said.

But it added: "In the fire no one has died or been injured." Firemen had stopped the spread of the blaze, which also affected a pumping station and directly threatened eight supply tanks holding more than 10,000 tonnes of petrol.

The refinery was formerly owned by Czech company Chemopetrol a.s.. But under a recent deal bringing in the foreign oil consortium it was split away from the rest of the Litvinov petrochemical complex and handed to Ceska Rafinerska, which is 51 percent state-owned.

However, Chemopetrol spokesman Jan Martinek said output had been severely cut back at the complex. "For now production is running only slightly," he told CTK, adding that further decisions on output would depend on how it was possible to localise the fire.
